briefdescription.para: Function pointer to call for setbuf() functionality (changing the internal buffering on stdio calls).

detaileddescription.para: The library calls this function to disable buffering when reading or writing sensitive data, to avoid having extra copies of sensitive data remaining in stdio buffers after the file is closed. If this is not a concern, for example if your platform's stdio doesn't have any buffering, you can set mbedtls_setbuf to a function that does nothing. The library always calls this function with buf equal to NULL.

memberdef.name: mbedtls_platform_get_entropy

briefdescription.para: User defined callback function that is used from the entropy module to gather entropy data from some hardware device.

parameterdescription.para: A mask of PSA_DRIVER_GET_ENTROPY_xxx flags. As of TF-PSA-Crypto 1.0, this is always 0.
Measure of the entropy content (in bits) of the data written in the output buffer.
Output buffer where the entropy data will be stored.
Size of the output buffer in bytes.
The value of flags is not supported.

simplesect.para: For the time being TF-PSA-Crypto only supports implementations that return a maximum entropy output on each call, i.e. estimate_bits = 8 * output_size. Returning a smaller entropy content is the same as returning PSA_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_ENTROPY so the hardware polling will fail. In the future TF-PSA-Crypto will be smarter and capable to cope with entropy sources with lower entropy content (i.e. 0 < estimate_bits < 8 * output_size) by calling the callback function in loop.

briefdescription.para: This file contains the definitions and functions of the Mbed TLS platform abstraction layer.

detaileddescription.para: The platform abstraction layer removes the need for the library to directly link to standard C library functions or operating system services, making the library easier to port and embed. Application developers and users of the library can provide their own implementations of these functions, or implementations specific to their platform, which can be statically linked to the library or dynamically configured at runtime.
When all compilation options related to platform abstraction are disabled, this header just defines mbedtls_xxx function names as aliases to the standard xxx function.
Most modules in the library and example programs are expected to include this header.
